Animal biotech poised for 44% jump in
free cash flow by 2026
Agtech may have inched up just 6% last quarter,
but animal agriculture names blasted 16%
higher—headlined by Atlantic Sapphire, whose
US land-based salmon comeback sent its stock
up a staggering 109%. A 15% tariff on Norwegian
imports and record cattle and hog prices only
sweetened the story. On the policy front, US
President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill
Act restored 100% bonus depreciation and
research & development expensing, yet its
subsidy tilt toward megafarmers could crimp
near-term demand for smaller-scale agtech
solutions.
The outlook stays bullish on the biology side:
Analysts peg animal agriculture revenue growth
at 13% for 2025 and 20% for 2026, with gross
margins widening from 26% to 42%. In animal
biotech, EBITDA growth is set to accelerate to
8% next year, and median free cash flow is on
track to soar 44%—with Genus and Elanco
leading the margin charge. Get the full metrics,
trend drivers, and IPO watch list in our latest
deep-dive report.

Valuation Guide tracks metrics for key publicly
